text: Why does the Elowitz-Leibler repressilator require an odd number of repressors (three, in the original design) arranged in a closed ring?
choices: An odd number of repressive steps around the loop produces net negative feedback, a prerequisite (with nonlinearity and delay) for sustained oscillation
An even number of repressors would exceed standard plasmid cloning capacity
Odd numbers of repressors reduce metabolic burden on the host cell
Odd numbers of repressors are required so that dCas9 can multiplex several sgRNAs
explanation: An odd number of repressive (inverting) links around a closed loop yields net negative feedback overall, which combined with sufficient nonlinearity (high Hill coefficient) and a time delay (from protein synthesis) is a requirement for sustained oscillations; an even number would instead create net positive feedback, favoring bistability rather than oscillation. Cloning capacity and metabolic burden are unrelated to the odd/even repressor count, and dCas9 multiplexing is a feature of CRISPR-based logic gates, not a requirement of oscillator topology.
